+        sorted_masses = sorted(self._masses[self._mass_order[j]]
+                               for j in range(self._num_cubes))
+
+        per_cube_status = ["unplaced"] * self._num_cubes
+        any_off_table = False
+
+        for i in range(self._num_cubes):
+            try:
+                body_name = "cube_main" if i == 0 else f"cube_{i}_main"
+                body_id = sim.model.body_name2id(body_name)
+                pos = sim.data.body_xpos[body_id]
+            except Exception:
+                continue
+
+            if pos[2] < self._failure_floor_threshold:
+                any_off_table = True

+            # Only table-resting cubes can be "placed". Held/transiting
+            # cubes stay "unplaced" even if their xy overlaps a zone.
+            on_table = (
+                self._table_height - self._cube_size
+                <= pos[2]
+                <= self._table_height + 2 * self._cube_size
+            )
+            if not on_table:
+                continue
+
+            target_zone = sorted_masses.index(self._masses[self._mass_order[i]])
+
+            for z in range(self._num_cubes):
+                try:
+                    zone_id = sim.model.body_name2id(f"zone_{z}_main")
+                except Exception:
+                    continue
+                zone_pos = sim.data.body_xpos[zone_id]
+                if np.linalg.norm(pos[:2] - zone_pos[:2]) < self._zone_width / 2:
+                    per_cube_status[i] = "correct" if z == target_zone else "wrong"
+                    break  # each cube can overlap at most one zone
+
+        return per_cube_status, any_off_table

+        """Score = fraction of cubes currently in their correct zone."""
+        statuses, _ = self._cube_zone_state()
+        return sum(s == "correct" for s in statuses) / max(1, self._num_cubes)
+

+        """Terminate only on full success or any wrong placement / off-table.
+
+        - All cubes ``"correct"``  → success, reward 1.
+        - Any cube  ``"wrong"``    → failure, reward 0.
+        - Any cube off the table   → failure, reward 0.
+        - Mix of ``"correct"`` and ``"unplaced"`` → keep going.
+        """
+        statuses, any_off_table = self._cube_zone_state()
+        if all(s == "correct" for s in statuses):
+            self._last_outcome = "success"
+            self._last_reason = "all cubes placed in their correct zones"
+            return True
+        if any_off_table:
+            self._last_outcome = "failure"
+            self._last_reason = (
+                f"a cube fell off the table (z < {self._failure_floor_threshold})"
+            )
+            return True
+        if any(s == "wrong" for s in statuses):
+            wrong_idxs = [i for i, s in enumerate(statuses) if s == "wrong"]
+            colors = [self.CUBE_COLORS[i % len(self.CUBE_COLORS)][0] for i in wrong_idxs]
+            self._last_outcome = "failure"
+            self._last_reason = f"wrong-zone placement: {', '.join(colors)}"
+            return True
+        self._last_outcome = None
+        self._last_reason = None
+        return False
+

+        """Binary reward: 1.0 on success, 0.0 otherwise (including failure)."""
+        obs, _reward, terminated, truncated, info = super().step(action)
+        reward = 1.0 if (terminated and self._last_outcome == "success") else 0.0
+        info["outcome"] = self._last_outcome
+        info["reason"] = self._last_reason
+        if terminated:
+            # Dump the per-cube ground-truth mapping so wrong-zone
+            # failures are self-explanatory.
+            statuses, _ = self._cube_zone_state()
+            sim = self._env.sim
+            sorted_masses = sorted(self._masses[self._mass_order[j]]
+                                   for j in range(self._num_cubes))
+            details = []
+            for i in range(self._num_cubes):
+                color = self.CUBE_COLORS[i % len(self.CUBE_COLORS)][0]
+                mass_g = int(round(self._masses[self._mass_order[i]] * 1000))
+                target = sorted_masses.index(self._masses[self._mass_order[i]])
+                # Find which zone (if any) this cube is inside, and its
+                # distance to the *target* zone so near-misses are visible.
+                bname = "cube_main" if i == 0 else f"cube_{i}_main"
+                in_zone = "-"
+                d_to_target = float("nan")
+                z_rel_to_table = float("nan")
+                try:
+                    bid = sim.model.body_name2id(bname)
+                    cpos = sim.data.body_xpos[bid]
+                    z_rel_to_table = cpos[2] - self._table_height
+                    for z in range(self._num_cubes):
+                        zpos = sim.data.body_xpos[sim.model.body_name2id(f"zone_{z}_main")]
+                        if np.linalg.norm(cpos[:2] - zpos[:2]) < self._zone_width / 2:
+                            in_zone = str(z)
+                            break
+                    tgt_pos = sim.data.body_xpos[sim.model.body_name2id(f"zone_{target}_main")]
+                    d_to_target = float(np.linalg.norm(cpos[:2] - tgt_pos[:2]))
+                except Exception:
+                    in_zone = "?"
+                details.append(
+                    f"{color}({mass_g}g)→target=zone_{target} in=zone_{in_zone} "
+                    f"d={d_to_target*100:.1f}cm z={z_rel_to_table*100:.1f}cm "
+                    f"[{statuses[i]}]"
+                )

+                "[MassSortV1] step=%d  reward=%.1f  outcome=%s  reason: %s\n    cubes: %s",
+                self._step_count, reward, self._last_outcome,
+                self._last_reason, " | ".join(details),
+            )
+        elif truncated:
+            logger.info(
+                "[MassSortV1] step=%d  reward=%.1f  outcome=truncated  "
+                "reason: hit max_episode_steps (%d), task_score=%.3f",
+                self._step_count, reward, self.MAX_EPISODE_STEPS,
+                info.get("task_score", 0.0),
+            )
+        return obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info

+"""Mirror Pick Place — pick up a cube off the table to a target lift height.
+
+Task ID: ``ib-m-mirror-pick-place-v1``
+"""
+
+import numpy as np
+from imbench.tasks.prehensile.single_arm_base import SingleArmBase
+
+
+class MirrorPickPlaceV1(SingleArmBase):
+    TASK_ID = "ib-m-mirror-pick-place-v1"
+    DESCRIPTION = (
+        "Single arm: pick up a cube lying on the table and lift it to a "
+        "target height. Cube position and color are randomized each reset."
+    )
+
+    def _parse_task_config(self):
+        task_cfg = self.cfg.get("task", {})
+        self._cube_size = task_cfg.get("cube_size", 0.02)
+        self._cube_mass = task_cfg.get("cube_mass", 0.05)
+        self._lift_height = task_cfg.get("lift_height", 0.1)
+
+    def _make_objects(self):
+        return [
+            {"type": "box", "name": "cube",
+             "size": [self._cube_size] * 3,
+             "rgba": [0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0],
+             "density": self._cube_mass / (8 * self._cube_size ** 3),
+             "friction": [1.0, 0.005, 0.0001],
+             "joints": "default"},
+        ]
+
+    def reset(self, *, seed=None, options=None):
+        obs, info = super().reset(seed=seed, options=options)
+
+        # Randomize cube color (independent of the visual-randomization
+        # flag so this task always has a varying cube color).
+        sim = self._env.sim
+        cube_body_id = sim.model.body_name2id("cube_main")
+        geom_start = sim.model.body_geomadr[cube_body_id]
+        geom_count = sim.model.body_geomnum[cube_body_id]
+        rgba = self._random_object_color()
+        for gi in range(geom_start, geom_start + geom_count):
+            sim.model.geom_rgba[gi] = rgba
+
+        sim.forward()
+        obs = self._rebuild_obs()
+        self._flip_cameras(obs)
+        return obs, info
+
+    def step(self, action):
+        obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = super().step(action)
+        self._flip_cameras(obs)
+        return obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info
+
+    def _flip_cameras(self, obs):
+        # Flip every camera frame both horizontally and vertically
+        # (equivalent to a 180° rotation in the image plane). The
+        # bird-eye camera is exempt — its top-down view is unaffected
+        # by the in-plane flip the task uses to mirror the scene.
+        for key in list(obs.keys()):
+            if not (key.startswith("rgb_") or key.startswith("depth_")):
+                continue
+            if "bird" in key:
+                continue
+            obs[key] = obs[key][::-1, ::-1]
+
+    def _compute_task_score(self, raw_obs):
+        if "cube_pos" not in raw_obs:
+            return 0.0
+        cube_z = raw_obs["cube_pos"][2]
+        lift = cube_z - self._table_height
+        return 1.0 if lift >= self._lift_height else 0.0
+
+    def _check_termination(self, raw_obs):
+        if self._compute_task_score(raw_obs) >= self._success_score_threshold:
+            return True
+        return self._object_fell_off_table(raw_obs)

+"""Occluder Push — push plates aside to find the red cube and place it on the green patch.

+"""
+
+import numpy as np
+from imbench.tasks.prehensile.single_arm_base import SingleArmBase
+
+
+class OccluderPushV1(SingleArmBase):
+    TASK_ID = "ib-p5-occluder-push-v1"
+    DESCRIPTION = "Single arm: Find the red cube and place it on the green patch."
+
+    def _parse_task_config(self):
+        task_cfg = self.cfg.get("task", {})
+        self._patch_pos = np.array(task_cfg.get("patch_pos", [-0.10, 0.0]))
+        self._patch_tolerance = task_cfg.get("placement_threshold", 0.04)
+        self._cube_size = task_cfg.get("cube_size", 0.02)
+        self._lid_thickness = task_cfg.get("lid_thickness", 0.005)
+        self._lid_half_size = task_cfg.get("lid_half_size", 0.06)
+        self._num_distractors = task_cfg.get("num_distractors", 2)
+        self._cube_placed = False
+
+    def _make_objects(self):
+        """Red target cube + distractor cubes + one lid per cube."""
+        objects = [
+            # Target (red)
+            {"type": "box", "name": "cube",
+             "size": [self._cube_size] * 3,
+             "rgba": [0.8, 0.2, 0.2, 1.0],
+             "density": 100, "friction": [0.8, 0.005, 0.0001],
+             "joints": "default"},
+            # Lid for the target cube
+            {"type": "box", "name": "lid",
+             "size": [self._lid_half_size, self._lid_half_size,
+                      self._lid_thickness],
+             "rgba": [0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 1.0],
+             "density": 200, "friction": [0.4, 0.005, 0.0001],
+             "joints": "default"},
+        ]
+        # Distractor cubes + their lids
+        distractor_colors = [
+            [0.2, 0.5, 0.9, 1.0],   # blue
+            [0.9, 0.7, 0.1, 1.0],   # yellow
+            [0.6, 0.2, 0.8, 1.0],   # purple
+            [1.0, 0.5, 0.1, 1.0],   # orange
+        ]
+        for i in range(self._num_distractors):
+            objects.append({
+                "type": "box",
+                "name": f"distractor_{i}",
+                "size": [self._cube_size] * 3,
+                "rgba": distractor_colors[i % len(distractor_colors)],
+                "density": 100, "friction": [0.8, 0.005, 0.0001],
+                "joints": "default",
+            })
+            objects.append({
+                "type": "box",
+                "name": f"lid_{i}",
+                "size": [self._lid_half_size, self._lid_half_size,
+                         self._lid_thickness],
+                "rgba": [0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 1.0],
+                "density": 200, "friction": [0.4, 0.005, 0.0001],
+                "joints": "default",
+            })
+        return objects
+
+    def _make_static_objects(self):
+        return [
+            # Green patch — placement target (flat visual marker)
+            {"type": "box", "name": "goal_patch",
+             "size": [0.05, 0.05, 0.001],
+             "rgba": [0.2, 0.7, 0.2, 0.5],
+             "density": 1000, "friction": [0.5, 0.005, 0.0001],
+             "joints": None},
+        ]
+
+    def reset(self, *, seed=None, options=None):
+        obs, info = super().reset(seed=seed, options=options)
+        self._cube_placed = False
+
+        total_cubes = 1 + self._num_distractors  # target + distractors
+
+        # Generate shuffled positions for all hidden cubes
+        positions = self._generate_cube_positions(total_cubes)
+        # Randomly assign slots; index 0 = red target cube
+        slot_order = list(range(total_cubes))
+        self._rng.shuffle(slot_order)
+        target_slot = slot_order[0]
+
+        # Place target cube + lid
+        cx, cy = positions[target_slot]
+        cube_z = self._table_height + self._cube_size + 0.005
+        self._place_object("cube", [cx, cy, cube_z])
+        lid_z = cube_z + self._cube_size + self._lid_thickness + 0.001
+        self._place_object("lid", [cx, cy, lid_z])
+
+        # Place distractor cubes + their lids
+        for i in range(self._num_distractors):
+            slot = slot_order[1 + i]
+            dx, dy = positions[slot]
+            self._place_object(f"distractor_{i}", [dx, dy, cube_z])
+            lid_z_d = cube_z + self._cube_size + self._lid_thickness + 0.001
+            self._place_object(f"lid_{i}", [dx, dy, lid_z_d])
+
+        # Place the green patch
+        self._place_static("goal_patch", [
+            self._patch_pos[0], self._patch_pos[1],
+            self._table_height + 0.001,
+        ])
+
+        self._env.sim.forward()
+        obs = self._rebuild_obs()
+        return obs, info
+
+    def _generate_cube_positions(self, n):
+        """Return *n* non-overlapping (x, y) positions in the workspace."""
+        positions = []
+        min_sep = self._lid_half_size * 2 + 0.04  # avoid lid overlap
+        for _ in range(n):
+            for _attempt in range(200):
+                x = 0.12 + self._rng.uniform(-0.06, 0.06)
+                y = self._rng.uniform(-0.10, 0.10)
+                if all(np.hypot(x - px, y - py) > min_sep
+                       for px, py in positions):
+                    positions.append((x, y))
+                    break
+            else:
+                # Fallback: just place it (may overlap slightly)
+                positions.append((x, y))
+        return positions
+
+    def _compute_task_score(self, raw_obs):
+        """Binary score: 1.0 iff red cube rests on the green patch, else 0.0."""
+        if "cube_pos" not in raw_obs:
+            return 0.0
+        cube_xy = raw_obs["cube_pos"][:2]
+        cube_z = raw_obs["cube_pos"][2]
+        dist_to_patch = np.linalg.norm(cube_xy - self._patch_pos)
+        if (dist_to_patch < self._patch_tolerance
+                and cube_z < self._table_height + 0.05):
+            self._cube_placed = True
+            return 1.0
+        return 0.0
+
+    def _check_termination(self, raw_obs):
+        if self._cube_placed:
+            return True
+        return self._object_fell_off_table(raw_obs)
+
+    def step(self, action):
+        """Binary reward: 1.0 on success, 0.0 otherwise (including off-table failure)."""
+        obs, _reward, terminated, truncated, info = super().step(action)
+        reward = 1.0 if (terminated and self._cube_placed) else 0.0
+        return obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info

+"""Packing Problem (Tetris-style) — single-arm suction puzzle task.
+
+The flat region just inside the bin is decomposed by a Bin-Packing-Problem
+generator (Algorithm 2 from the BPP literature: recursively split an item
+along a random axis at a random position, weighted by volume / edge length).
+The decomposition produces 8 axis-aligned boxes that tile the inner shape,
+which are then fused pairwise into 4 L-shaped pieces. A single Panda arm
+fitted with a suction gripper picks, rotates, and places each L-piece
+flat inside the bin.
+
+Task ID: ``ib-p7-packing-v1``
+"""
+
+import numpy as np
+
+import imbench.envs  # noqa: F401
+import imbench.grippers  # noqa: F401  — registers PandaSuctionGripper
+from imbench.grippers.suction_weld import SuctionWeld
+from imbench.objects import EXTRAS_DIR, ExtrasObject
+from imbench.tasks.base_task import BaseTask, load_task_config
+
+
+# All XYZ dimensions are scaled by 2× compared to the original packing_box
+# (which had inner 0.18 × 0.12 m, depth 0.015 m).
+_SCALE = 2.0
+
+# Packing box inner half-extents (drives both the generated bin XML and the
+# in-bin success check).
+_BOX_INNER_HALF_X = 0.09 * _SCALE
+_BOX_INNER_HALF_Y = 0.06 * _SCALE
+_BOX_WALL_THICK = 0.005 * _SCALE
+_BOX_WALL_HEIGHT = 0.015 * _SCALE
+_BOX_BASE_THICK = 0.005 * _SCALE   # = 2 × 0.0025
+
+# Inner flat shape — slightly smaller than the bin interior so pieces fit.
+_INNER_MARGIN = 0.005 * _SCALE
+_INNER_L = 2 * (_BOX_INNER_HALF_X - _INNER_MARGIN)   # along x
+_INNER_W = 2 * (_BOX_INNER_HALF_Y - _INNER_MARGIN)   # along y
+_PIECE_THICKNESS = 0.01 * _SCALE                      # along z
+
+# Default range for the number of L-shaped pieces. The actual count is
+# sampled per-episode (see ``randomization.piece_count_range`` in the YAML).
+_DEFAULT_PIECE_COUNT_RANGE = (3, 4)
+_MAX_PIECES = 4  # upper bound so we can pre-allocate dynamic-object slots
+
+# Minimum sub-box edge length so pieces remain graspable.
+_MIN_EDGE = 0.018 * _SCALE
+
+# XY shrink factor applied to every sub-box just before MJCF generation.
+# Each sub-box is scaled around its own centre, so the BPP tiling layout
+# is preserved but neighbours no longer share full faces — a ~2.5 % gap
+# of edge length on each side prevents spawn-time wedging.
+_PIECE_XY_SHRINK = 0.90
+
+# A piece counts as "settled" only after it has held contact with the bin
+# (any wall / base) for this many consecutive sim steps while NOT being
+# held by suction. Stops the success check from firing while the cup is
+# still descending — the welded piece is geometrically inside the bin
+# and flat at that point, but it isn't really packed yet.
+_PIECE_SETTLED_CONTACT_STEPS = 50
+
+# Color palette for the 4 L-pieces.
+_PIECE_COLORS = [
+    (0.10, 0.80, 0.85, 1.0),  # cyan
+    (0.95, 0.55, 0.20, 1.0),  # orange
+    (0.45, 0.85, 0.30, 1.0),  # green
+    (0.85, 0.30, 0.55, 1.0),  # magenta
+]
+
+# Asset name for the scaled bin (regenerated on import — idempotent).
+_BIN_ASSET = "packing_box_2x"
+
+
+def _bin_xml() -> str:
+    """Render the open-top rectangular bin as MJCF, scaled to 2×."""
+    hx = _BOX_INNER_HALF_X + _BOX_WALL_THICK            # outer half-x
+    hy = _BOX_INNER_HALF_Y + _BOX_WALL_THICK            # outer half-y
+    base_h = _BOX_BASE_THICK / 2                        # base half-thickness
+    wall_hh = _BOX_WALL_HEIGHT / 2                      # wall half-height
+    wall_z = _BOX_BASE_THICK + wall_hh                  # wall centre z (above base)
+    color = "0.55 0.45 0.30 1"
+    return f"""<mujoco model="{_BIN_ASSET}">
+  <compiler angle="radian"/>
+  <worldbody>
+    <body>
+      <body name="object" pos="0 0 0">
+        <!-- Base plate -->
+        <geom name="vis" type="box" size="{hx} {hy} {base_h}"

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+#  BPP decomposition
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def _bpp_split_rectangles(L: float, W: float, n: int, rng: np.random.RandomState):
+    """Split a flat rectangle of size (L, W) into ``n`` axis-aligned rects.
+
+    Implements Algorithm 2 (BPP generator) restricted to 2D guillotine splits:
+    while we have fewer than n items, pop one weighted by area, choose an axis
+    weighted by edge length, and split it at a random position weighted by
+    distance to the edge centre. ``_MIN_EDGE`` keeps every child graspable.
+
+    Returns a list of ``(cx, cy, lx, ly)`` tuples (centre + full extents).
+    """
+    # Each item: [cx, cy, lx, ly]
+    items = [[0.0, 0.0, L, W]]
+    while len(items) < n:
+        areas = np.array([it[2] * it[3] for it in items])
+        # Weighted pop by area. Skip items that can't be split further.
+        splittable = np.array([
+            (it[2] >= 2 * _MIN_EDGE) or (it[3] >= 2 * _MIN_EDGE)
+            for it in items
+        ])
+        weights = areas * splittable
+        if weights.sum() <= 0:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "BPP split: no item large enough to split further. "
+                "Decrease _MIN_EDGE or the number of pieces."
+            )
+        idx = rng.choice(len(items), p=weights / weights.sum())
+        cx, cy, lx, ly = items.pop(idx)
+
+        # Choose axis weighted by edge length, restricted to splittable axes.
+        axis_weights = np.array([
+            lx if lx >= 2 * _MIN_EDGE else 0.0,
+            ly if ly >= 2 * _MIN_EDGE else 0.0,
+        ])
+        axis = rng.choice(2, p=axis_weights / axis_weights.sum())
+
+        edge = lx if axis == 0 else ly
+        # Split position weighted by distance to centre (Algorithm 2). Use a
+        # triangular density peaked at the edges, clamped to leave both
+        # children >= _MIN_EDGE.
+        lo = _MIN_EDGE
+        hi = edge - _MIN_EDGE
+        # Sample with bias toward the centre via a Beta(1.5, 1.5)-ish dist;
+        # this matches "distance to centre" weighting from the paper.
+        u = rng.beta(1.5, 1.5)
+        pos = lo + u * (hi - lo)
+
+        if axis == 0:
+            l1, l2 = pos, edge - pos
+            c1 = cx - lx / 2 + l1 / 2
+            c2 = cx - lx / 2 + l1 + l2 / 2
+            items.append([c1, cy, l1, ly])
+            items.append([c2, cy, l2, ly])
+        else:
+            l1, l2 = pos, edge - pos
+            c1 = cy - ly / 2 + l1 / 2
+            c2 = cy - ly / 2 + l1 + l2 / 2
+            items.append([cx, c1, lx, l1])
+            items.append([cx, c2, lx, l2])
+    return items
+
+
+def _are_adjacent(a, b, tol: float = 1e-6):
+    """Two axis-aligned rects are adjacent if they share a face segment.
+
+    Returns the shared axis (0 = vertical edge, 1 = horizontal edge) and the
+    overlap length, or ``None`` if not adjacent.
+    """
+    ax_lo, ax_hi = a[0] - a[2] / 2, a[0] + a[2] / 2
+    ay_lo, ay_hi = a[1] - a[3] / 2, a[1] + a[3] / 2
+    bx_lo, bx_hi = b[0] - b[2] / 2, b[0] + b[2] / 2
+    by_lo, by_hi = b[1] - b[3] / 2, b[1] + b[3] / 2
+
+    # Shared vertical edge (touching along x)
+    if abs(ax_hi - bx_lo) < tol or abs(bx_hi - ax_lo) < tol:
+        overlap = min(ay_hi, by_hi) - max(ay_lo, by_lo)
+        if overlap > tol:
+            return 0, overlap
+    # Shared horizontal edge (touching along y)
+    if abs(ay_hi - by_lo) < tol or abs(by_hi - ay_lo) < tol:
+        overlap = min(ax_hi, bx_hi) - max(ax_lo, bx_lo)
+        if overlap > tol:
+            return 1, overlap
+    return None
+
+
+def _union_is_rectangle(a, b, tol: float = 1e-6):
+    """Two adjacent boxes union into a rectangle iff they share the full edge."""
+    res = _are_adjacent(a, b, tol)
+    if res is None:
+        return False
+    axis, overlap = res
+    if axis == 0:
+        return abs(overlap - min(a[3], b[3])) < tol and abs(a[3] - b[3]) < tol
+    return abs(overlap - min(a[2], b[2])) < tol and abs(a[2] - b[2]) < tol
+
+
+def _pair_into_l_shapes(boxes, rng: np.random.RandomState):
+    """Match adjacent sub-boxes into pairs whose union is L-shaped.
+
+    Backtracking search over all valid perfect matchings of the adjacency
+    graph that uses only L-shape edges (adjacent + non-rectangular union).
+    Falls back to allowing rectangular unions if no all-L matching exists.
+
+    Returns a list of (box_a, box_b) pairs.
+    """
+    n = len(boxes)
+    assert n % 2 == 0
+    # Precompute edge sets.
+    l_neighbors = {i: [] for i in range(n)}
+    any_neighbors = {i: [] for i in range(n)}
+    for i in range(n):
+        for j in range(i + 1, n):
+            if _are_adjacent(boxes[i], boxes[j]) is None:
+                continue
+            any_neighbors[i].append(j)
+            any_neighbors[j].append(i)
+            if not _union_is_rectangle(boxes[i], boxes[j]):
+                l_neighbors[i].append(j)
+                l_neighbors[j].append(i)
+
+    def _search(neighbors):
+        order = list(range(n))
+        rng.shuffle(order)
+        used = [False] * n
+        pairs_idx: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
+
+        def recurse():
+            i = next((k for k in order if not used[k]), None)
+            if i is None:
+                return True
+            cands = [j for j in neighbors[i] if not used[j]]
+            rng.shuffle(cands)
+            for j in cands:
+                used[i] = used[j] = True
+                pairs_idx.append((i, j))
+                if recurse():
+                    return True
+                pairs_idx.pop()
+                used[i] = used[j] = False
+            return False
+
+        return pairs_idx if recurse() else None
+
+    matched = _search(l_neighbors)
+    if matched is None:
+        raise RuntimeError("BPP pairing: no all-L matching for this split.")
+    return [(boxes[i], boxes[j]) for i, j in matched]
+
+
+def _generate_l_pieces(rng: np.random.RandomState, num_pieces: int):
+    """Build ``num_pieces`` L-shaped pieces tiling the inner rectangle.
+
+    Strategy: BPP-split the inner rectangle into ``2 * num_pieces`` axis-
+    aligned boxes, then greedily pair adjacent boxes (preferring L-unions).
+    Retries with fresh splits if a pairing has no L-shaped candidates left.
+
+    Returns a list of dicts, each describing one L-piece:
+        {
+          "subboxes": [(cx, cy, lx, ly), (cx, cy, lx, ly)],  # in inner-rect frame
+          "centroid": (cx, cy),                               # area-weighted centroid
+          "color":    (r, g, b, a),
+        }
+    """
+    if num_pieces < 1:
+        raise ValueError(f"num_pieces must be >= 1, got {num_pieces}")
+    num_subboxes = 2 * num_pieces
+    last_err = None
+    for _ in range(50):
+        try:
+            boxes = _bpp_split_rectangles(_INNER_L, _INNER_W, num_subboxes, rng)
+            pairs = _pair_into_l_shapes(boxes, rng)
+            break
+        except RuntimeError as e:
+            last_err = e
+            continue
+    else:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to generate L-pieces: {last_err}")
+
+    pieces = []
+    for k, (a, b) in enumerate(pairs):
+        # Shrink the whole L around its own centroid, not each sub-box around
+        # its own centre. Scaling each sub-box independently opens a gap at
+        # the shared interior edge — the L develops a notch and stops being
+        # an L. Scaling positions AND sizes uniformly about the centroid
+        # keeps the shared edge glued (both sub-boxes' touching faces map to
+        # the same line under a homothety) while the outer perimeter pulls
+        # inward, giving the desired gap from neighbouring pieces.
+        area_a = a[2] * a[3]
+        area_b = b[2] * b[3]
+        l_cx = (a[0] * area_a + b[0] * area_b) / (area_a + area_b)
+        l_cy = (a[1] * area_a + b[1] * area_b) / (area_a + area_b)
+        s = _PIECE_XY_SHRINK
+        a = (
+            l_cx + (a[0] - l_cx) * s,
+            l_cy + (a[1] - l_cy) * s,
+            a[2] * s, a[3] * s,
+        )
+        b = (
+            l_cx + (b[0] - l_cx) * s,
+            l_cy + (b[1] - l_cy) * s,
+            b[2] * s, b[3] * s,
+        )
+        # Recompute centroid from the shrunk boxes (it equals the homothety
+        # centre by construction, but recomputing keeps the data consistent
+        # with subboxes for downstream consumers).
+        area_a = a[2] * a[3]
+        area_b = b[2] * b[3]
+        cx = (a[0] * area_a + b[0] * area_b) / (area_a + area_b)
+        cy = (a[1] * area_a + b[1] * area_b) / (area_a + area_b)
+        # Authoritative grasp anchor for scripted suction-pick policies:
+        # the centre of the sub-box with the **largest minimum edge
+        # length** — i.e. the most "blocky" of the two. A circular
+        # suction snout (radius ~15 mm) needs both the x- and y-half-
+        # extents of its target sub-box to clear the snout radius, so
+        # picking by max(min(lx, ly)) avoids long thin bars where the
+        # snout would overhang the short edge. The area-weighted
+        # centroid above sits at the inside corner of the L — empty
+        # space — so it's not itself a usable grasp point.
+        anchor_sub = a if min(a[2], a[3]) >= min(b[2], b[3]) else b
+        grasp_x, grasp_y = anchor_sub[0], anchor_sub[1]
+        pieces.append({
+            "subboxes": [tuple(a), tuple(b)],
+            "centroid": (cx, cy),
+            "grasp_anchor": (grasp_x, grasp_y),
+            "color": _PIECE_COLORS[k % len(_PIECE_COLORS)],
+        })
+    return pieces
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+#  MJCF generation
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def _l_piece_xml(model_name: str, piece: dict) -> str:
+    """Render an L-piece as MuJoCo XML (two box geoms in a free body).
+
+    Sub-box positions are expressed relative to the piece centroid so the
+    piece's body origin sits at the geometric centre of mass.
+    """
+    cx, cy = piece["centroid"]
+    r, g, b, a = piece["color"]
+    geoms = []
+    for k, (sx, sy, lx, ly) in enumerate(piece["subboxes"]):
+        # Relative to centroid, lift by half-thickness so body Z=0 is bottom.
+        gx, gy = sx - cx, sy - cy
+        gz = _PIECE_THICKNESS / 2
+        hx, hy, hz = lx / 2, ly / 2, _PIECE_THICKNESS / 2
+        geoms.append(
+            f'<geom name="vis_{k}" type="box" size="{hx} {hy} {hz}" '
+            f'pos="{gx} {gy} {gz}" rgba="{r} {g} {b} {a}" '
+            f'group="1" contype="0" conaffinity="0"/>'
+        )
+        geoms.append(
+            f'<geom name="col_{k}" type="box" size="{hx} {hy} {hz}" '
+            f'pos="{gx} {gy} {gz}" rgba="{r} {g} {b} {a}" group="0"/>'
+        )
+    geoms_xml = "\n        ".join(geoms)
+
+    # Half-extents of the bounding box around both sub-boxes (for sites).
+    xs_lo = min(sx - lx / 2 for (sx, sy, lx, ly) in piece["subboxes"])
+    xs_hi = max(sx + lx / 2 for (sx, sy, lx, ly) in piece["subboxes"])
+    ys_lo = min(sy - ly / 2 for (sx, sy, lx, ly) in piece["subboxes"])
+    ys_hi = max(sy + ly / 2 for (sx, sy, lx, ly) in piece["subboxes"])
+    bbox_hx = max(abs(xs_lo - cx), abs(xs_hi - cx))
+    bbox_hy = max(abs(ys_lo - cy), abs(ys_hi - cy))
+
+    return f"""<mujoco model="{model_name}">
+  <compiler angle="radian"/>
+  <worldbody>
+    <body>
+      <body name="object" pos="0 0 0">
+        {geoms_xml}
+        <inertial pos="0 0 {_PIECE_THICKNESS / 2}" mass="0.05"
+                  diaginertia="0.00001 0.00001 0.00002"/>
+      </body>
+      <site rgba="0 0 0 0" size="0.005" pos="0 0 0" name="bottom_site"/>
+      <site rgba="0 0 0 0" size="0.005" pos="0 0 {_PIECE_THICKNESS}" name="top_site"/>
+      <site rgba="0 0 0 0" size="0.005" pos="{bbox_hx} {bbox_hy} 0" name="horizontal_radius_site"/>
+    </body>
+  </worldbody>
+</mujoco>
+"""
+
+
+def _write_l_piece_assets(pieces: list[dict], tag) -> list[str]:
+    """Write an XML file per piece into ``deps/extras/`` and return asset names.
+
+    ``tag`` is mixed into the filename so multiple PackingV1 instances (or
+    repeated reset() calls within one process) don't collide on disk.
+    """
+    asset_names = []
+    for k, piece in enumerate(pieces):
+        name = f"packing_lpiece_{tag}_{k}"
+        path = EXTRAS_DIR / f"{name}.xml"
+        path.write_text(_l_piece_xml(name, piece))
+        asset_names.append(name)
+    return asset_names
+

+class PackingV1(BaseTask):
+    """Packing puzzle: pack 4 procedurally-generated L-pieces into a box."""
+
+    TASK_ID = "ib-p7-packing-v1"
+    DESCRIPTION = (
+        "Pack 4 procedurally-generated L-shaped flat blocks (decomposed from "
+        "the bin's inner shape via a BPP generator) into the rectangular bin."
+    )
+
+    def __init__(self, task_id: str = None, **kwargs):
+        if task_id:
+            self.TASK_ID = task_id
+        self.CONFIG_FILE = f"prehensile/{self.TASK_ID}"
+
+        _cfg = load_task_config(self.TASK_ID, config_file=self.CONFIG_FILE)
+        self.DESCRIPTION = _cfg.get("description", self.DESCRIPTION)
+        if "max_episode_steps" in _cfg:
+            self.MAX_EPISODE_STEPS = _cfg["max_episode_steps"]
+
+        self._rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
+
+        # Randomization config
+        rand_cfg = _cfg.get("randomization", {})
+        place_cfg = rand_cfg.get("block_placement", {})
+        self._rand_block_placement = place_cfg.get("enabled", False)
+        self._place_x_range = place_cfg.get("x_range", 0.10)
+        self._place_y_range = place_cfg.get("y_range", 0.10)
+
+        yaw_cfg = rand_cfg.get("block_yaw", {})
+        self._rand_block_yaw = yaw_cfg.get("enabled", False)
+
+        # Per-episode L-shape count, sampled from this inclusive range. The
+        # env is rebuilt on each reset() so a different number / shape of
+        # L-pieces is presented every episode.
+        pc_range = rand_cfg.get("piece_count_range", _DEFAULT_PIECE_COUNT_RANGE)
+        self._piece_count_range = (int(pc_range[0]), int(pc_range[-1]))
+        if not (1 <= self._piece_count_range[0] <= self._piece_count_range[1] <= _MAX_PIECES):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"piece_count_range {self._piece_count_range} must satisfy "
+                f"1 <= lo <= hi <= {_MAX_PIECES}"
+            )
+
+        # Scene config
+        scene_cfg = _cfg.get("scene", {})
+        self._table_color = scene_cfg.get("table_color", [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0])
+        # Task-specific parameters live under `task:` per the prehensile
+        # YAML convention; fall back to root for backwards compatibility.
+        task_cfg = _cfg.get("task", {})
+        self._box_pos = task_cfg.get(
+            "fixture_pos", _cfg.get("fixture_pos", [0.0, 0.0]),
+        )
+
+        table_cfg = scene_cfg.get("table", {})
+        self._table_height = table_cfg.get("height", 0.9)
+        _full_size = table_cfg.get("full_size")
+        self._table_full_size = tuple(_full_size) if _full_size else (1.0, 0.75, 0.05)
+        _offset = table_cfg.get("offset")
+        self._table_offset = tuple(_offset) if _offset else (0, 0, self._table_height)
+
+        _robot_offset = scene_cfg.get("robot_offset")
+        self._robot_offset = [list(r) for r in _robot_offset] if _robot_offset else None
+
+        cond_cfg = _cfg.get("task_conditions", {})
+        success_cfg = cond_cfg.get("success", {})
+        self._success_score_threshold = success_cfg.get("score_threshold", 1.0)
+        failure_cfg = cond_cfg.get("failure", {})
+        self._failure_floor_threshold = failure_cfg.get("floor_z_threshold", 0.05)
+
+        light_cfg = rand_cfg.get("lighting", {})
+        self._rand_light_position = light_cfg.get("position", False)
+        self._rand_light_color = light_cfg.get("color", False)
+
+        # Per-instance tag for asset filenames so multiple PackingV1
+        # instances (or repeated reset() rewrites) don't clobber each other.
+        self._asset_tag = f"t{id(self):x}"
+
+        # Generate the initial L-pieces from the configured seed. The env
+        # is rebuilt on each reset() with a fresh BPP split (and possibly
+        # a different piece count), so this initial generation just decides
+        # how many dynamic-object slots the first env build gets.
+        self._gen_seed = kwargs.get("seed", 0)
+        gen_rng = np.random.RandomState(self._gen_seed)
+        n0 = self._sample_piece_count(gen_rng)
+        self._pieces, self._block_asset_names = self._generate_pieces(
+            self._gen_seed, n0,
+        )
+
+        # Suction weld is contact-driven; reset cache between episodes.
+        self._suction_weld = SuctionWeld()
+
+        super().__init__(**kwargs)
+
+    def _sample_piece_count(self, rng: np.random.RandomState) -> int:
+        lo, hi = self._piece_count_range
+        return int(rng.randint(lo, hi + 1))
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _piece_bbox_half(piece: dict) -> tuple[float, float]:
+        """Return (hx, hy) bounding-box half-extents around the piece centroid."""
+        cx, cy = piece["centroid"]
+        xs_lo = min(sx - lx / 2 for (sx, sy, lx, ly) in piece["subboxes"])
+        xs_hi = max(sx + lx / 2 for (sx, sy, lx, ly) in piece["subboxes"])
+        ys_lo = min(sy - ly / 2 for (sx, sy, lx, ly) in piece["subboxes"])
+        ys_hi = max(sy + ly / 2 for (sx, sy, lx, ly) in piece["subboxes"])
+        return max(abs(xs_lo - cx), abs(xs_hi - cx)), max(abs(ys_lo - cy), abs(ys_hi - cy))
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _piece_bbox_directional(piece: dict) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]:
+        """Return signed half-extents (h_left, h_right, h_down, h_up) around centroid.
+
+        Unlike :meth:`_piece_bbox_half` (which returns symmetric ``max(abs(…))``),
+        this gives the *directional* reach so the spawn logic can place a piece
+        right against an obstacle on one side without leaving extra slack on
+        the other.
+        """
+        cx, cy = piece["centroid"]
+        xs_lo = min(sx - lx / 2 for (sx, sy, lx, ly) in piece["subboxes"])
+        xs_hi = max(sx + lx / 2 for (sx, sy, lx, ly) in piece["subboxes"])
+        ys_lo = min(sy - ly / 2 for (sx, sy, lx, ly) in piece["subboxes"])
+        ys_hi = max(sy + ly / 2 for (sx, sy, lx, ly) in piece["subboxes"])
+        return cx - xs_lo, xs_hi - cx, cy - ys_lo, ys_hi - cy
+
+    def _generate_pieces(self, seed: int, num_pieces: int):
+        gen_rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
+        pieces = _generate_l_pieces(gen_rng, num_pieces)
+        asset_names = _write_l_piece_assets(pieces, self._asset_tag)
+        return pieces, asset_names
+
+    def _build_env(self, **kwargs):
+        use_cameras = self.obs_mode in ("rgb", "combo") and self.has_cameras
+
+        self._block_names = [f"lpiece_{k}" for k in range(len(self._block_asset_names))]
+        block_specs = [
+            {"type": "extras", "name": name, "extras_name": asset,
+             "joints": "default"}
+            for name, asset in zip(self._block_names, self._block_asset_names)
+        ]
+        box_spec = {"type": "extras", "name": "packing_box",
+                    "extras_name": _BIN_ASSET, "joints": None}
+
+        common_kwargs = dict(
+            robots="Panda",
+            gripper_types="PandaSuctionGripper",
+            control_freq=self.control_freq,
+            controller_configs=self.controller_configs,
+            has_renderer=(self.render_mode == "human"),
+            has_offscreen_renderer=use_cameras,
+            render_camera=None,
+            use_camera_obs=use_cameras,
+            camera_names=self._camera_names() if use_cameras else None,
+            camera_heights=self._camera_heights() if use_cameras else 84,
+            camera_widths=self._camera_widths() if use_cameras else 84,
+            horizon=self.MAX_EPISODE_STEPS,
+        )
+
+        # Rotate the arm 90° clockwise (around table centre) so its workspace
+        # spans the table's long axis (X) — pieces scattered on both sides
+        # of the bin along ±X are then within reach. Without this the arm
+        # sits on the -X side and can only reach the -X column.
+        if self._robot_offset is not None:
+            robot_offset = self._robot_offset[0]
+        else:
+            import robosuite.utils.transform_utils as T
+            from robosuite.models.robots import Panda
+            default_xpos = np.array(
+                Panda().base_xpos_offset["table"](self._table_full_size[0])
+            )
+            rot = np.array([0.0, 0.0, np.pi / 2])
+            rotated_xpos = T.euler2mat(rot) @ default_xpos
+            robot_offset = list(rotated_xpos) + list(rot)
+
+        env = self._make_robosuite_env(
+            "SingleArmTableEnv",
+            objects=block_specs,
+            static_objects=[box_spec],
+            table_full_size=self._table_full_size,
+            table_offset=self._table_offset,
+            robot_offset=robot_offset,
+            placement_config={
+                "x_range": [0.0, 0.0],
+                "y_range": [0.0, 0.0],
+                "z_offset": 0.01,
+                "reference_pos": [0.0, 0.0, self._table_height],
+                "ensure_valid_placement": False,
+            },
+            **common_kwargs,
+        )
+
+        # Cache MujocoObject handles for downstream qpos / scoring lookups.
+        self._blocks = list(env._dynamic_objects)
+        self._box = env.get_object("packing_box")
+        return env
+
+    def _get_block_positions(self):
+        positions = {}
+        for name, block in zip(self._block_names, self._blocks):
+            bid = self._env.sim.model.body_name2id(block.root_body)
+            positions[name] = np.array(self._env.sim.data.body_xpos[bid])
+        return positions
+
+    def _block_in_box(self, block_pos, box_pos):
+        dx = abs(block_pos[0] - box_pos[0])
+        dy = abs(block_pos[1] - box_pos[1])
+        # Vertical containment: piece centre must sit between the bin floor
+        # and the wall rim, with a half-piece-thickness of slack so a piece
+        # resting on the floor is "in" and one floating above the rim is not.
+        floor_z = box_pos[2] + _BOX_BASE_THICK
+        rim_z = floor_z + _BOX_WALL_HEIGHT
+        z_lo = floor_z - _PIECE_THICKNESS / 2
+        z_hi = rim_z + _PIECE_THICKNESS / 2
+        in_z = z_lo < block_pos[2] < z_hi
+        return dx < _BOX_INNER_HALF_X and dy < _BOX_INNER_HALF_Y and in_z
+
+    def _block_is_flat(self, block):
+        bid = self._env.sim.model.body_name2id(block.root_body)
+        quat = self._env.sim.data.body_xquat[bid]
+        w, x, y, z = quat
+        up_z = 1 - 2 * (x * x + y * y)
+        tilt_angle = np.arccos(np.clip(abs(up_z), 0, 1))
+        return tilt_angle < np.deg2rad(5.0)
+
+    def reset(self, *, seed=None, options=None):
+        self._suction_weld.reset()
+
+        # ── Per-episode regeneration ─────────────────────────────────
+        # Re-run BPP with a new seed, sample a new piece count, and
+        # rebuild the underlying robosuite env so the new geometry takes
+        # effect. The seed is taken from the BaseTask seed (set via
+        # reset(seed=...) or constructor) so episodes are reproducible.
+        # We do this BEFORE super().reset() so the new env state flows
+        # through the parent's observation pipeline correctly.
+        episode_seed = seed if seed is not None else getattr(self, "seed", 0)
+        regen_rng = np.random.RandomState(episode_seed)
+        n_pieces = self._sample_piece_count(regen_rng)
+        # Use a high-entropy split-seed derived from episode_seed so the
+        # BPP layout differs across seeds and across attempts.
+        split_seed = int(regen_rng.randint(0, 2**31 - 1))
+        self._pieces, self._block_asset_names = self._generate_pieces(
+            split_seed, n_pieces,
+        )
+        # Tear down the previous env and rebuild with the new asset list.
+        if getattr(self, "_env", None) is not None:
+            self._env.close()
+        self._env = self._build_env()
+        # Re-apply post-build patches that BaseTask.__init__ runs only once:
+        # the suction-camera fix mutates the freshly-loaded MuJoCo XML, so
+        # without re-running it the rebuilt env reverts to the default
+        # eye_in_hand pose that the pump body occludes.
+        if self._custom_cameras:
+            self._inject_custom_cameras()
+        self._fix_suction_eye_in_hand()
+
+        obs, info = super().reset(seed=seed, options=options)
+        if seed is not None:
+            self._rng = np.random.RandomState(self.seed)
+
+        sim = self._env.sim
+        table_z = self._env.table_offset[2]
+
+        # Place box fixture
+        box_bid = self._env.sim.model.body_name2id(self._box.root_body)
+        box_pos = np.array([
+            self._box_pos[0], self._box_pos[1],
+            table_z + abs(self._box.bottom_offset[2]) + 0.001,
+        ])
+        sim.model.body_pos[box_bid] = box_pos
+
+        # Scatter L-pieces on the table around the bin. Clearance is
+        # computed per-piece from its directional bounding box so the
+        # piece's edge nearest the bin sits a controlled distance away
+        # from the bin wall — no spawn-time intersection or visual
+        # overlap, regardless of which way the centroid is biased.
+        bin_half_x = _BOX_INNER_HALF_X + _BOX_WALL_THICK
+        bin_half_y = _BOX_INNER_HALF_Y + _BOX_WALL_THICK
+        gap = 0.06  # clearance between piece's near edge and bin wall
+
+        for i, (block, piece) in enumerate(zip(self._blocks, self._pieces)):
+            phx, phy = self._piece_bbox_half(piece)
+            hl, hr, hd, hu = self._piece_bbox_directional(piece)
+            if self._rand_block_placement:
+                bx = self._rng.uniform(-self._place_x_range, self._place_x_range)
+                by = self._rng.uniform(-self._place_y_range, self._place_y_range)
+                while (abs(bx - self._box_pos[0]) < bin_half_x + phx + gap
+                       and abs(by - self._box_pos[1]) < bin_half_y + phy + gap):
+                    bx = self._rng.uniform(-self._place_x_range, self._place_x_range)
+                    by = self._rng.uniform(-self._place_y_range, self._place_y_range)
+            else:
+                # Alternate +X / -X side; rows step along Y on each side.
+                # Use *directional* extents so the piece's near edge (the
+                # one facing the bin) sits exactly ``gap`` from the wall.
+                side = 1 if (i % 2 == 0) else -1
+                row = i // 2
+                near_extent = hl if side == 1 else hr  # extent toward bin
+                bx = self._box_pos[0] + side * (bin_half_x + gap + near_extent)
+                # Stagger rows along Y; centre the row stack on the bin.
+                by = self._box_pos[1] + (row - 0.5) * (2 * phy + gap)
+
+            bz = table_z + abs(block.bottom_offset[2]) + 0.002
+            block_pos = np.array([bx, by, bz])
+
+            if self._rand_block_yaw:
+                yaw = self._rng.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi)
+                quat = np.array([np.cos(yaw / 2), 0, 0, np.sin(yaw / 2)])
+            else:
+                quat = np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0])
+
+            sim.data.set_joint_qpos(
+                block.joints[0],
+                np.concatenate([block_pos, quat]),
+            )
+
+        if self._rand_light_position or self._rand_light_color:
+            for i in range(sim.model.nlight):
+                if self._rand_light_position:
+                    sim.model.light_pos[i] = [
+                        self._rng.uniform(0.0, 2.0),
+                        self._rng.uniform(-1.0, 2.0),
+                        self._rng.uniform(1.0, 2.5),
+                    ]
+                if self._rand_light_color:
+                    base = self._rng.uniform(0.75, 1.0)
+                    sim.model.light_diffuse[i] = np.clip(
+                        base + self._rng.uniform(-0.05, 0.05, size=3), 0.6, 1.0,
+                    )
+
+        self._block_fell_off = False
+
+        # Per-piece bin-contact streaks (reset to zero whenever the piece
+        # loses contact with the bin or is welded to suction). A piece
+        # only counts as "settled in the bin" once its streak reaches
+        # _PIECE_SETTLED_CONTACT_STEPS — the success check requires this
+        # for every piece on top of the geometric in-box / flat checks.
+        self._bin_contact_streak: dict[str, int] = {
+            name: 0 for name in self._block_names
+        }
+        # Cache body ids used for contact filtering. Populated lazily in
+        # step() the first time it runs (after env build).
+        self._packing_box_body_id: int | None = None
+        self._block_body_ids: dict[str, int] = {}
+
+        sim.forward()
+
+        self._camera_cache.clear()
+        raw_obs = self._get_sim_observations(force_update=True)
+        self._inject_ft_sensor(raw_obs)
+        self._inject_tactile_obs(raw_obs)
+        obs = self._get_obs(raw_obs)
+        info = {"task_score": 0.0, "step": 0}
+        return obs, info
+
+    def step(self, action):
+        result = super().step(action)
+        # Drive suction-weld activation/release after the physics step so
+        # contact data reflects the post-step state.
+        self._suction_weld.update(self._env, action)
+        # Update per-piece bin-contact streaks. Done after the suction
+        # update so the welded_body_id check reflects this tick's state.
+        self._update_bin_contact_streaks()
+        return result
+
+    def _welded_body_ids(self) -> set[int]:
+        """Body ids currently held by any suction weld this episode."""
+        ids: set[int] = set()
+        for handles in self._suction_weld._handles.values():
+            if handles.welded_body_id is not None:
+                ids.add(int(handles.welded_body_id))
+        return ids
+
+    def _update_bin_contact_streaks(self) -> None:
+        """Increment each piece's bin-contact streak if it has at least
+        one MuJoCo contact with the packing box AND is not held by
+        suction; otherwise reset its streak to zero.
+        """
+        sim = self._env.sim
+
+        # Lazy-cache body ids on the first call after a fresh env build.
+        if self._packing_box_body_id is None:
+            self._packing_box_body_id = sim.model.body_name2id(
+                self._box.root_body)
+            self._block_body_ids = {
+                name: sim.model.body_name2id(block.root_body)
+                for name, block in zip(self._block_names, self._blocks)
+            }
+
+        box_bid = self._packing_box_body_id
+        welded = self._welded_body_ids()
+        # Block-id → still-touching-bin? (default False, flipped True on
+        # first matching contact this step)
+        in_contact = {name: False for name in self._block_names}
+
+        ncon = int(sim.data.ncon)
+        for i in range(ncon):
+            c = sim.data.contact[i]
+            b1 = int(sim.model.geom_bodyid[int(c.geom1)])
+            b2 = int(sim.model.geom_bodyid[int(c.geom2)])
+            if b1 != box_bid and b2 != box_bid:
+                continue
+            other = b2 if b1 == box_bid else b1
+            for name, bbid in self._block_body_ids.items():
+                if bbid == other:
+                    in_contact[name] = True
+                    break
+
+        for name, bbid in self._block_body_ids.items():
+            if in_contact[name] and bbid not in welded:
+                self._bin_contact_streak[name] += 1
+            else:
+                self._bin_contact_streak[name] = 0
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+    #  Solution preview
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    def solution_image(self, width: int = 480, height: int = 360) -> np.ndarray:
+        """Render the goal layout (4 L-pieces tiling the bin) as an RGB image.
+
+        Used by ``scripts/collect_demos.py`` to show the operator what the
+        target configuration looks like, since the L-shapes are procedurally
+        generated and the operator can't infer the layout otherwise.
+
+        Returns
+        -------
+        np.ndarray
+            ``(H, W, 3)`` uint8 RGB array suitable for cv2.imshow / writeText.
+        """
+        # We do everything with numpy + a tiny rasteriser so this works
+        # headless and without a matplotlib import (matplotlib's heavy state
+        # would clash with the inline dashboard's window manager).
+        img = np.full((height, width, 3), 245, dtype=np.uint8)
+
+        # World→pixel mapping. Fit the bin's outer footprint with 8 % padding.
+        outer_x = _BOX_INNER_HALF_X + _BOX_WALL_THICK
+        outer_y = _BOX_INNER_HALF_Y + _BOX_WALL_THICK
+        pad = 0.08
+        sx = (1 - 2 * pad) * width / (2 * outer_x)
+        sy = (1 - 2 * pad) * height / (2 * outer_y)
+        scale = min(sx, sy)
+        cx_px, cy_px = width // 2, height // 2
+
+        def w2p(x, y):
+            # Flip y so +y is up in the image (visual convention).
+            return (
+                int(round(cx_px + x * scale)),
+                int(round(cy_px - y * scale)),
+            )
+
+        def fill_rect(cx, cy, lx, ly, rgb):
+            x0, y1 = w2p(cx - lx / 2, cy - ly / 2)
+            x1, y0 = w2p(cx + lx / 2, cy + ly / 2)
+            x0, x1 = sorted((x0, x1))
+            y0, y1 = sorted((y0, y1))
+            x0, y0 = max(x0, 0), max(y0, 0)
+            x1, y1 = min(x1, width), min(y1, height)
+            img[y0:y1, x0:x1] = rgb
+
+        def stroke_rect(cx, cy, lx, ly, rgb, thickness=2):
+            x0, y1 = w2p(cx - lx / 2, cy - ly / 2)
+            x1, y0 = w2p(cx + lx / 2, cy + ly / 2)
+            x0, x1 = sorted((x0, x1))
+            y0, y1 = sorted((y0, y1))
+            x0, y0 = max(x0, 0), max(y0, 0)
+            x1, y1 = min(x1, width), min(y1, height)
+            t = thickness
+            img[y0:y0 + t, x0:x1] = rgb
+            img[y1 - t:y1, x0:x1] = rgb
+            img[y0:y1, x0:x0 + t] = rgb
+            img[y0:y1, x1 - t:x1] = rgb
+
+        # Bin walls (outer outline + inner outline).
+        wood = np.array([141, 116, 77], dtype=np.uint8)  # warm wood
+        stroke_rect(0, 0, 2 * outer_x, 2 * outer_y, wood, thickness=4)
+        stroke_rect(0, 0, 2 * _BOX_INNER_HALF_X, 2 * _BOX_INNER_HALF_Y, wood,
+                    thickness=2)
+
+        # Each L-piece: fill its 2 sub-boxes, then a thin border around them.
+        for piece in self._pieces:
+            r, g, b, _ = piece["color"]
+            rgb = np.array([int(r * 255), int(g * 255), int(b * 255)], dtype=np.uint8)
+            for (sxc, syc, lx, ly) in piece["subboxes"]:
+                fill_rect(sxc, syc, lx, ly, rgb)
+            for (sxc, syc, lx, ly) in piece["subboxes"]:
+                stroke_rect(sxc, syc, lx, ly, (rgb // 2).astype(np.uint8),
+                            thickness=1)
+        return img
+
+    def __del__(self):
+        # Best-effort cleanup of any per-instance XML assets we wrote.
+        # Match by asset_tag so we also remove files from prior reset()
+        # generations that aren't in the current _block_asset_names list.
+        try:
+            tag = getattr(self, "_asset_tag", None)
+            if tag is None:
+                return
+            for p in EXTRAS_DIR.glob(f"packing_lpiece_{tag}_*.xml"):
+                try:
+                    p.unlink()
+                except Exception:
+                    pass
+        except Exception:
+            pass
+
+    def _get_obs(self, raw_obs):
+        obs = self._build_obs_from_config(raw_obs)
+
+        if self.object_state_enabled:
+            for block in self._blocks:
+                pf = block.naming_prefix
+                if f"{pf}pos" in raw_obs:
+                    obs[f"{pf}pos"] = raw_obs[f"{pf}pos"]
+                if f"{pf}quat" in raw_obs:
+                    obs[f"{pf}quat"] = raw_obs[f"{pf}quat"]
+
+        return obs
+
+    def _compute_task_score(self, raw_obs):
+        # All-or-nothing: 1.0 only when every piece is geometrically in
+        # the bin AND lying flat AND has been in contact with the bin
+        # for at least _PIECE_SETTLED_CONTACT_STEPS sim steps while not
+        # held by suction. The contact-streak requirement stops the
+        # check from firing while the cup is still descending — the
+        # welded piece is geometrically in-box and flat at that point
+        # but isn't actually packed yet.
+        box_bid = self._env.sim.model.body_name2id(self._box.root_body)
+        box_pos = self._env.sim.data.body_xpos[box_bid]
+
+        positions = self._get_block_positions()
+
+        for name, block in zip(self._block_names, self._blocks):
+            pos = positions[name]
+            if not (self._block_in_box(pos, box_pos)
+                    and self._block_is_flat(block)
+                    and self._bin_contact_streak.get(name, 0)
+                        >= _PIECE_SETTLED_CONTACT_STEPS):
+                return 0.0
+        return 1.0
+
+    def _check_termination(self, raw_obs):
+        if self._compute_task_score(raw_obs) >= self._success_score_threshold:
+            return True
+        # Failure: any piece dropped off the table.  We trigger as soon as
+        # the piece centre is below the table top by more than a small
+        # margin (it can't recover from there) instead of waiting for it
+        # to hit the floor — fail fast, save the operator's time.
+        table_z = self._env.table_offset[2]
+        drop_margin = 0.05  # metres below table top
+        positions = self._get_block_positions()
+        for pos in positions.values():
+            if pos[2] < table_z - drop_margin or pos[2] < self._failure_floor_threshold:
+                self._block_fell_off = True
+                return True
+        return False

+"""Pendulum Grasp — time a grasp to catch a swinging sphere at the apex.
+
+Task ID: ``ib-p2-pendulum-grasp-v1``
+"""
+
+import numpy as np
+from imbench.tasks.prehensile.single_arm_base import SingleArmBase
+
+
+class PendulumGraspV1(SingleArmBase):
+    TASK_ID = "ib-p2-pendulum-grasp-v1"
+    DESCRIPTION = (
+        "Single arm: a sphere swings on an ideal (undamped) pendulum. "
+        "Time the grasp to catch it within 1 cm of the swing apex."
+    )
+
+    APEX_TOLERANCE = 0.01  # 1 cm — strict tolerance for the grasp branch
+
+    # ── "Resting on gripper" success branch ──────────────────────────
+    # If the bob ended up balanced on top of the closed gripper (rather
+    # than pinched between the jaws), the grasp check fails but we still
+    # count it as a success when:
+    #   - bob's Z is above the EEF site by RESTING_Z_OVER_EEF_MIN
+    #   - bob's horizontal offset from the EEF is within RESTING_XY_TOL
+    #   - bob is approximately stationary (|v_hinge| < RESTING_VEL_TOL)
+    #   - bob's Z is within RESTING_APEX_TOL of apex_z
+    RESTING_Z_OVER_EEF_MIN = 0.0     # m, bob centroid must be ≥ EEF z
+    RESTING_XY_TOL         = 0.06    # m, horizontal distance EEF↔bob
+    RESTING_VEL_TOL        = 0.05    # rad/s, hinge angular velocity
+    RESTING_APEX_TOL       = 0.04    # m, looser apex_z window (4 cm)
+
+    def _parse_task_config(self):
+        task_cfg = self.cfg.get("task", {})
+        rand_cfg = self.cfg.get("randomization", {}).get("pendulum", {})
+
+        # Build-time geometry: sampled once per env construction (XML is
+        # baked in _make_static_objects). If a randomization range is
+        # given, sample within it; otherwise use the task default.
+        def _sample_or_default(key, default):
+            rng = rand_cfg.get(key)
+            if isinstance(rng, (list, tuple)) and len(rng) == 2:
+                return float(self._rng.uniform(*rng))
+            return float(task_cfg.get(key, default))
+
+        self._arm_length = _sample_or_default("pendulum_length", 0.70)
+        self._stand_height = _sample_or_default("frame_height", 0.85)
+        self._bob_size = _sample_or_default("bob_size", 0.025)
+
+        # Swing amplitude is sampled per-reset from this range.
+        self._swing_amplitude_range = task_cfg.get(
+            "swing_amplitude_range", [15, 45]
+        )
+        # Damping range is sampled per-reset (mutated on sim.model.dof_damping).
+        self._damping_range = rand_cfg.get("pendulum_damping")
+        self._bob_shape = task_cfg.get("bob_shape", "sphere")
+        self._damping = float(task_cfg.get("pendulum_damping", 0.0))
+
+        self._grasped = False
+        self._apex_z = None
+
+    def _make_objects(self):
+        # No free-joint dynamic objects — the bob is part of the pendulum
+        return []
+
+    def _make_static_objects(self):
+        return [
+            {"type": "pendulum", "name": "pendulum",
+             "stand_height": self._stand_height,
+             "arm_length": self._arm_length,
+             "bob_size": self._bob_size,
+             "bob_shape": self._bob_shape,
+             "bob_rgba": [0.2, 0.2, 0.8, 1.0],
+             "damping": self._damping,
+             "joints": None},
+        ]
+
+
+    def reset(self, *, seed=None, options=None):
+        obs, info = super().reset(seed=seed, options=options)
+        self._grasped = False
+
+        sim = self._env.sim
+
+        # Position the pendulum stand on the table.
+        # Stand is at the far end (large x); bracket extends toward robot
+        # (-x), so the bob swings closer to the robot with the stand behind it.
+        stand_x = 0.17
+        stand_y = 0.0
+        stand_z = self._table_height
+        self._place_static("pendulum", [stand_x, stand_y, stand_z])
+
+        # Set initial hinge angle to create the swing
+        amplitude = np.radians(
+            self._rng.uniform(*self._swing_amplitude_range)
+        )
+        try:
+            hinge_name = "pendulum_hinge"
+            joint_id = sim.model.joint_name2id(hinge_name)
+            qpos_addr = sim.model.jnt_qposadr[joint_id]
+            dof_addr = sim.model.jnt_dofadr[joint_id]
+            sim.data.qpos[qpos_addr] = amplitude
+            sim.data.qvel[dof_addr] = 0.0
+            # Per-reset damping randomization (live-mutable on the model).
+            if isinstance(self._damping_range, (list, tuple)) and len(self._damping_range) == 2:
+                damp = float(self._rng.uniform(*self._damping_range))
+                sim.model.dof_damping[dof_addr] = damp
+        except Exception:
+            pass
+
+        # Apex z: with the bob released from amplitude θ on an ideal
+        # pendulum, energy conservation makes |θ| = amplitude at every
+        # swing extreme. Bob centre traces a radius (arm_length + bob_size)
+        # from the pivot; pivot height = stand_z + stand_height.
+        pivot_z = stand_z + self._stand_height
+        radius = self._arm_length + self._bob_size
+        self._apex_z = pivot_z - radius * np.cos(amplitude)
+
+        # Fix gripper collision geometry for pendulum grasping:
+        # 1. Enable collision on fingerpads so _check_grasp can detect contact
+        #    (Panda pads default to contype=0 which prevents any MuJoCo contact)
+        # 2. Disable conaffinity on finger bodies and palm so the bob can swing freely
+        #    into the pad gap without being physically blocked by the gripper body mesh.
+        for pad_name in [
+            "gripper0_right_finger1_pad_collision",
+            "gripper0_right_finger2_pad_collision",
+        ]:
+            try:
+                gid = sim.model.geom_name2id(pad_name)
+                sim.model.geom_contype[gid] = 1
+                sim.model.geom_conaffinity[gid] = 1
+            except Exception:
+                pass
+        for body_name in [
+            "gripper0_right_finger1_collision",
+            "gripper0_right_finger2_collision",
+            "gripper0_right_hand_collision",
+        ]:
+            try:
+                gid = sim.model.geom_name2id(body_name)
+                sim.model.geom_conaffinity[gid] = 0
+            except Exception:
+                pass
+
+        # Per-reset bob color randomization (the pendulum is static, so
+        # the standard color-randomization path in SingleArmBase doesn't
+        # touch it — apply directly to the bob geom).
+        if self._rand_object_color:
+            try:
+                gid = sim.model.geom_name2id("pendulum_bob")
+                sim.model.geom_rgba[gid] = self._random_object_color()
+            except Exception:
+                pass
+
+        sim.forward()
+        obs = self._rebuild_obs()
+        return obs, info
+
+    def _get_bob_pos(self):
+        """Get the bob geom center position from sim."""
+        sim = self._env.sim
+        try:
+            gid = sim.model.geom_name2id("pendulum_bob")
+            return sim.data.geom_xpos[gid].copy()
+        except Exception:
+            return None
+
+    def _get_bob_quat(self):
+        """Get the bob geom orientation as xyzw quat from sim."""
+        sim = self._env.sim
+        try:
+            gid = sim.model.geom_name2id("pendulum_bob")
+            xmat = sim.data.geom_xmat[gid].reshape(3, 3)
+            from robosuite.utils.transform_utils import mat2quat
+            return mat2quat(xmat)  # returns xyzw
+        except Exception:
+            return None
+
+    def _get_obs(self, raw_obs):
+        obs = super()._get_obs(raw_obs)
+        bob_pos = self._get_bob_pos()
+        if bob_pos is not None:
+            obs["object_pos"] = bob_pos
+        bob_quat = self._get_bob_quat()
+        if bob_quat is not None:
+            obs["object_quat"] = bob_quat
+        return obs
+
+    def _compute_task_score(self, raw_obs):
+        try:
+            is_grasping = self._check_grasp(
+                gripper=self._env.robots[0].gripper,
+                object_geoms=["pendulum_bob"],
+            )
+        except (AttributeError, RuntimeError):
+            is_grasping = False
+
+        bob_pos = self._get_bob_pos()
+        if bob_pos is None or self._apex_z is None:
+            return 0.0
+
+        # ── Branch 1: bob is grasped between the jaws ──────────────
+        if is_grasping:
+            if abs(bob_pos[2] - self._apex_z) <= self.APEX_TOLERANCE:
+                self._grasped = True
+                return 1.0
+            return 0.5
+
+        # ── Branch 2: bob is resting on top of the gripper ─────────
+        # (jaws closed but bob sits above rather than between them).
+        eef_pos = raw_obs.get("robot0_eef_pos")
+        if eef_pos is None:
+            return 0.0
+        z_over_eef = float(bob_pos[2] - eef_pos[2])
+        xy_dist = float(np.linalg.norm(bob_pos[:2] - eef_pos[:2]))
+        # Hinge angular velocity → bob is "static" when the pendulum
+        # isn't actively swinging.
+        sim = self._env.sim
+        try:
+            joint_id = sim.model.joint_name2id("pendulum_hinge")
+            v_hinge = abs(float(sim.data.qvel[sim.model.jnt_dofadr[joint_id]]))
+        except Exception:
+            v_hinge = float("inf")
+
+        if (
+            z_over_eef >= self.RESTING_Z_OVER_EEF_MIN
+            and xy_dist <= self.RESTING_XY_TOL
+            and v_hinge <= self.RESTING_VEL_TOL
+            and abs(bob_pos[2] - self._apex_z) <= self.RESTING_APEX_TOL
+        ):
+            self._grasped = True
+            return 1.0
+
+        return 0.0
+
+    def _check_termination(self, raw_obs):
+        return bool(self._grasped)

+"""Pendulum Grasp — time a grasp to catch a swinging sphere at the apex.
+
+Task ID: ``ib-p2-pendulum-grasp-v1``
+"""
+
+import logging
+
+import numpy as np
+from imbench.tasks.prehensile.single_arm_base import SingleArmBase
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+class PendulumGraspV2(SingleArmBase):
+    TASK_ID = "ib-p2-pendulum-grasp-v2"
+    DESCRIPTION = (
+        "Single arm: a sphere swings on an ideal (undamped) pendulum. "
+        "Time the grasp to catch it within 1 cm of the swing apex."
+    )
+
+    APEX_TOLERANCE = 0.01  # 1 cm — strict tolerance for the grasp branch
+
+    # ── "Resting on gripper" success branch ──────────────────────────
+    # If the bob ended up balanced on top of the closed gripper (rather
+    # than pinched between the jaws), the grasp check fails but we still
+    # count it as a success when:
+    #   - bob's Z is above the EEF site by RESTING_Z_OVER_EEF_MIN
+    #   - bob's horizontal offset from the EEF is within RESTING_XY_TOL
+    #   - bob is approximately stationary (|v_hinge| < RESTING_VEL_TOL)
+    #   - bob's Z is within RESTING_APEX_TOL of apex_z
+    RESTING_Z_OVER_EEF_MIN = 0.0     # m, bob centroid must be ≥ EEF z
+    RESTING_XY_TOL         = 0.06    # m, horizontal distance EEF↔bob
+    RESTING_VEL_TOL        = 0.05    # rad/s, hinge angular velocity
+    RESTING_APEX_TOL       = 0.04    # m, looser apex_z window (4 cm)
+
+    def _parse_task_config(self):
+        task_cfg = self.cfg.get("task", {})
+        rand_cfg = self.cfg.get("randomization", {}).get("pendulum", {})
+
+        # Build-time geometry: sampled once per env construction (XML is
+        # baked in _make_static_objects). If a randomization range is
+        # given, sample within it; otherwise use the task default.
+        def _sample_or_default(key, default):
+            rng = rand_cfg.get(key)
+            if isinstance(rng, (list, tuple)) and len(rng) == 2:
+                return float(self._rng.uniform(*rng))
+            return float(task_cfg.get(key, default))
+
+        self._arm_length = _sample_or_default("pendulum_length", 0.70)
+        self._stand_height = _sample_or_default("frame_height", 0.85)
+        self._bob_size = _sample_or_default("bob_size", 0.025)
+
+        # Swing amplitude is sampled per-reset from this range.
+        self._swing_amplitude_range = task_cfg.get(
+            "swing_amplitude_range", [15, 45]
+        )
+        # Damping range is sampled per-reset (mutated on sim.model.dof_damping).
+        self._damping_range = rand_cfg.get("pendulum_damping")
+        self._bob_shape = task_cfg.get("bob_shape", "sphere")
+        self._damping = float(task_cfg.get("pendulum_damping", 0.0))
+
+        self._grasped = False
+        self._apex_z = None
+
+    def _make_objects(self):
+        # No free-joint dynamic objects — the bob is part of the pendulum
+        return []
+
+    def _make_static_objects(self):
+        return [
+            {"type": "pendulum", "name": "pendulum",
+             "stand_height": self._stand_height,
+             "arm_length": self._arm_length,
+             "bob_size": self._bob_size,
+             "bob_shape": self._bob_shape,
+             "bob_rgba": [0.2, 0.2, 0.8, 1.0],
+             "damping": self._damping,
+             "joints": None},
+        ]
+
+
+    def reset(self, *, seed=None, options=None):
+        obs, info = super().reset(seed=seed, options=options)
+        self._grasped = False
+
+        sim = self._env.sim
+
+        stand_x = 0.17 / np.sqrt(2)   # ≈ 0.120
+        stand_y = 0.17 / np.sqrt(2)   # ≈ 0.120
+        stand_z = self._table_height
+        self._place_static("pendulum", [stand_x, stand_y, stand_z])
+
+        # --- Rotate hinge axis to 45° diagonal in XY plane ---
+        try:
+            joint_id = sim.model.joint_name2id("pendulum_hinge")
+            # MuJoCo stores joint axis in jnt_axis as a flat array (n_joints * 3)
+            sim.model.jnt_axis[joint_id] = [0.7071068, 0.7071068, 0.0]
+        except Exception as e:
+            logger.warning("Could not set hinge axis: %s", e)
+
+        # Set initial hinge angle
+        amplitude = np.radians(self._rng.uniform(*self._swing_amplitude_range))
+        try:
+            hinge_name = "pendulum_hinge"
+            joint_id = sim.model.joint_name2id(hinge_name)
+            qpos_addr = sim.model.jnt_qposadr[joint_id]
+            dof_addr = sim.model.jnt_dofadr[joint_id]
+            sim.data.qpos[qpos_addr] = amplitude
+            sim.data.qvel[dof_addr] = 0.0
+            if isinstance(self._damping_range, (list, tuple)) and len(self._damping_range) == 2:
+                damp = float(self._rng.uniform(*self._damping_range))
+                sim.model.dof_damping[dof_addr] = damp
+        except Exception:
+            pass
+
+        pivot_z = stand_z + self._stand_height
+        radius = self._arm_length + self._bob_size
+        self._apex_z = pivot_z - radius * np.cos(amplitude)
+
+        # Gripper collision geometry
+        for pad_name in [
+            "gripper0_right_finger1_pad_collision",
+            "gripper0_right_finger2_pad_collision",
+        ]:
+            try:
+                gid = sim.model.geom_name2id(pad_name)
+                sim.model.geom_contype[gid] = 1
+                sim.model.geom_conaffinity[gid] = 1
+            except Exception:
+                pass
+        for body_name in [
+            "gripper0_right_finger1_collision",
+            "gripper0_right_finger2_collision",
+            "gripper0_right_hand_collision",
+        ]:
+            try:
+                gid = sim.model.geom_name2id(body_name)
+                sim.model.geom_conaffinity[gid] = 0
+            except Exception:
+                pass
+
+        if self._rand_object_color:
+            try:
+                gid = sim.model.geom_name2id("pendulum_bob")
+                sim.model.geom_rgba[gid] = self._random_object_color()
+            except Exception:
+                pass
+
+        sim.forward()
+        obs = self._rebuild_obs()
+        return obs, info
+
+    def _get_bob_pos(self):
+        """Get the bob geom center position from sim."""
+        sim = self._env.sim
+        try:
+            gid = sim.model.geom_name2id("pendulum_bob")
+            return sim.data.geom_xpos[gid].copy()
+        except Exception:
+            return None
+
+    def _get_bob_quat(self):
+        """Get the bob geom orientation as xyzw quat from sim."""
+        sim = self._env.sim
+        try:
+            gid = sim.model.geom_name2id("pendulum_bob")
+            xmat = sim.data.geom_xmat[gid].reshape(3, 3)
+            from robosuite.utils.transform_utils import mat2quat
+            return mat2quat(xmat)  # returns xyzw
+        except Exception:
+            return None
+
+    def _get_obs(self, raw_obs):
+        obs = super()._get_obs(raw_obs)
+        bob_pos = self._get_bob_pos()
+        if bob_pos is not None:
+            obs["object_pos"] = bob_pos
+        bob_quat = self._get_bob_quat()
+        if bob_quat is not None:
+            obs["object_quat"] = bob_quat
+        return obs
+
+    def _compute_task_score(self, raw_obs):
+        try:
+            is_grasping = self._check_grasp(
+                gripper=self._env.robots[0].gripper,
+                object_geoms=["pendulum_bob"],
+            )
+        except (AttributeError, RuntimeError):
+            is_grasping = False
+
+        bob_pos = self._get_bob_pos()
+        if bob_pos is None or self._apex_z is None:
+            return 0.0
+
+        # ── Branch 1: bob is grasped between the jaws ──────────────
+        if is_grasping:
+            if abs(bob_pos[2] - self._apex_z) <= self.APEX_TOLERANCE:
+                self._grasped = True
+                return 1.0
+            return 0.5
+
+        # ── Branch 2: bob is resting on top of the gripper ─────────
+        # (jaws closed but bob sits above rather than between them).
+        eef_pos = raw_obs.get("robot0_eef_pos")
+        if eef_pos is None:
+            return 0.0
+        z_over_eef = float(bob_pos[2] - eef_pos[2])
+        xy_dist = float(np.linalg.norm(bob_pos[:2] - eef_pos[:2]))
+        # Hinge angular velocity → bob is "static" when the pendulum
+        # isn't actively swinging.
+        sim = self._env.sim
+        try:
+            joint_id = sim.model.joint_name2id("pendulum_hinge")
+            v_hinge = abs(float(sim.data.qvel[sim.model.jnt_dofadr[joint_id]]))
+        except Exception:
+            v_hinge = float("inf")
+
+        if (
+            z_over_eef >= self.RESTING_Z_OVER_EEF_MIN
+            and xy_dist <= self.RESTING_XY_TOL
+            and v_hinge <= self.RESTING_VEL_TOL
+            and abs(bob_pos[2] - self._apex_z) <= self.RESTING_APEX_TOL
+        ):
+            self._grasped = True
+            return 1.0
+
+        return 0.0
+
+    def _check_termination(self, raw_obs):
+        return bool(self._grasped)
